verifications.claim: Men aged 18 through 25 in the United States are required to register with the Selective Service System (SSS) for a potential military draft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: All male U.S. citizens and immigrants between the ages of 18 and 25... are required to register (R1); most males between 18 and 25 years old are already required to register (R2); young men must register themselves within 30 days of turning 18 (R3); US men are eligible... when they turn 18... until 26 (R5); Almost all men who are 18-25 years old... must register (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the age range 18-25 for male registration requirement.

verifications.claim: A military draft is not currently active.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Active conscription ended in January 1973 (R1); The US has not had a draft since the Vietnam War (R2); all-volunteer military... since 1973 (R3); no draft has been called... last time... 1972 (R5); The United States has not had a draft since 1973 (R8)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm no active draft since 1973.

verifications.claim: Registration with the Selective Service System is mandatory for male citizens and immigrants aged 18-25.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: All male U.S. citizens and immigrants between the ages of 18 and 25 (R1); most males between 18 and 25 (R2); all men within 30 days of turning 18 (R5); U.S. citizens... Immigrants (legal permanent residents and undocumented immigrants) (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for male citizens and immigrants 18-25.

verifications.claim: Men must register with the Selective Service System within 30 days of turning 18.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Men must register within 30 days of turning 18 (R1); Men are expected to self-register within 30 days of their 18th birthdays (R2); young men must register themselves within 30 days of turning 18 (R3); all men within 30 days of turning 18 (R5)

verifications.claim: Selective Service System registration is required up until age 26.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: the agency accepts late registrations until age 26 (R2); Once you turn 26, you are no longer required to register (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm registration obligation extends to age 26 for late registration.

verifications.claim: Male U.S. citizens residing in the US must register with the Selective Service System.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: All male U.S. citizens... residing in the United States, are required (R1); Almost all men who are 18-25 years old and live in the United States must register... U.S. citizens (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated for male US citizens residing in US.

verifications.claim: Male immigrants including residents, refugees, and undocumented residing in the US must register with the Selective Service System.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: immigrants between the ages of 18 and 25, whether documented or undocumented but residing in the United States (R1); Immigrants (legal permanent residents and undocumented immigrants) Refugees and asylum seekers (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly include immigrants, undocumented, refugees.

verifications.claim: A 2026 federal law further ensures automatic registration of eligible men.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: following a proposed rule... under authority granted by Congress in the fiscal 2026 National Defense Authorization Act (R1); Congress approved automatic registration... as part of the 2026 National Defense Authorization Act (R2); Automatic Selective Service registration is beginning on Dec. 18, 2026 (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct reference to 2026 NDAA enabling automatic registration.

verifications.claim: People on active duty in the armed forces are exempt from Selective Service System registration while on duty.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: there are some exemptions such as those on active duty
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly lists active duty as exemption from registration.

verifications.claim: People in the military academies are exempt from Selective Service System registration while on duty.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No source mentions military academies specifically for registration exemption.

verifications.claim: High school students can have their induction postponed until graduation or until they turn 20.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: A high school student may have his induction postponed until he graduates or until he reaches age 20.
verifications.reasoning: Exact match in official SSS source.

verifications.claim: College students can have their induction postponed until the end of the semester.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: A college student may have his induction postponed until he finishes the current semester (R4); temporary postponement to finish a college semester (R5)

verifications.claim: College seniors can have their induction postponed until the end of the academic year.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: A college student may have his induction postponed until he finishes the current semester or, if a senior, the end of the academic year.

verifications.claim: Failure to register with the Selective Service System is a felony.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Failing to register... is a felony (R2); failing to register is actually a federal felony (R5); It is a federal felony (R8)

verifications.claim: Penalties for failure to register with the Selective Service System include up to five years in prison.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: punishable by up to five years in prison (R1); five years’ imprisonment (R2); up to 5 years in prison (R5)

verifications.claim: Penalties for failure to register with the Selective Service System include up to $250,000 in fines.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: fines of up to $250,000 (R1); fine up to $250,000 (R2); $250,000 in fines (R5)

verifications.claim: Penalties for failure to register with the Selective Service System include loss of eligibility for federal student loans.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: denied student loans (R2); federal student financial aid (R5); state-funded student financial aid (R8)

verifications.claim: Penalties for failure to register with the Selective Service System include loss of eligibility for training.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: denial of... federal job training programs
verifications.reasoning: R1 directly mentions federal job training programs.

verifications.claim: Penalties for failure to register with the Selective Service System include loss of eligibility for citizenship
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: citizenship if an immigrant (R1); US citizenship, if they are immigrants (R2); block or delay the naturalization process (R5); citizenship (R8)
